title: Data Quality Is the Compute Multiplier — Ari Morcos, DatologyAI

primary.label: AI Data Engineering
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 100%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk addresses data curation for LLM and VLM training broadly, not specific to any single application vertical. The methods (clean, curate, create, compose) are general-purpose data engineering techniques applicable across domains.

domains.label: Developer Platforms
domains.rationale: DatologyAI is positioned as a platform/tool that other model-building teams use to curate training data. The Arcee partnership exemplifies DatologyAI as a developer tool for teams building frontier models.

domains.label: Legal & Compliance
domains.rationale: The Thomson Reuters case study involves legal domain adaptation—mid-training on proprietary legal data and LegalBench evaluation. However, this is one customer example rather than the talk's core focus.

summary: Ari Morcos, CEO and co-founder of DatologyAI, presents data quality as the most underleveraged compute multiplier in AI model training. With compute scarcity worsening (H100 prices up ~40% from lows, reasoning models consuming ~8x more tokens), he argues that better data steepens the learning curve, yielding equivalent model performance at a fraction of the cost. DatologyAI operates as a "data refinery" with four stages: clean (heuristic filters, benchmark decontamination), curate (quality classifiers, taxonomy balancing, redundancy reduction, task distribution matching), create (synthetic data via rephrasing to augment diversity and scale), and compose (sequencing across training stages, continuous curricula). The foundational proof comes from Morcos's NeurIPS 2022 Outstanding Paper "Beyond neural scaling laws," showing data selection changes the scaling law exponent. Concrete proof points include: VLMs matching Qwen 3.5 4B with ~145x less training compute via curation alone; multilingual gains using only 8% multilingual tokens with cross-lingual transfer correlated to language similarity; Thomson Reuters gaining ~5 LegalBench points with <1% of pre-training budget and post-training effectiveness nearly tripling on mid-trained models; and Arcee's Trinity Large reaching open-frontier performance on 17T curated public tokens for under $20M total. Morcos emphasizes that repeating high-quality data beats showing low-quality data up to a threshold, and that data curation is a frontier research engineering problem requiring multi-axis scoring at peta-byte scale.
whyItMatters: These concepts form a coherent argument that data engineering is the most underleveraged lever in AI model training. The scaling law exponent modification provides the theoretical foundation—data selection doesn't just improve performance incrementally, it changes the fundamental compute-performance relationship. The compute multiplier thesis and compute scarcity dynamics provide the economic urgency. The four-stage refinery pipeline (clean, curate, create, compose) provides the engineering methodology to operationalize this insight, with each stage addressing a specific failure mode: contamination (clean), redundancy and distribution mismatch (curate), data scarcity (create), and stage isolation (compose). The concrete proof points—VLM Pareto frontier improvement, cross-lingual transfer, mid-training synergy, predictable scaling, and the Arcee frontier model under $20M—demonstrate that this framework works at production scale across modalities, languages, and domains. The synthetic rephrasing and model collapse avoidance concepts address the data scarcity problem that limits all curation efforts. Together, these concepts reframe data curation from a preprocessing step into a frontier research engineering discipline that determines whether teams can build competitive models within realistic compute budgets.
temporalContext: The video was published on July 31, 2026. The research was conducted as of August 23, 2026. The talk references the NeurIPS 2022 Outstanding Paper (December 2022) as foundational research. DatologyAI was founded in 2023. The Arcee Trinity Large was announced January 27, 2026, with the arXiv technical report published February 19, 2026. The DatologyAI-Arcee case study was published April 10, 2026. The Thomson Reuters partnership blog was published April 9, 2026, and Thomson Reuters launched their own 'Thomson' AI model on July 31, 2026—the same day as this video's publication. The compute scarcity dynamics (H100 pricing, reasoning model token consumption) reflect conditions as of mid-2026. The specific quantitative VLM and multilingual results presented in the talk appear to be from DatologyAI's ongoing internal research as of mid-2026, with no published papers yet for these specific benchmarks.
takeaways: Data quality is a compute multiplier: better data steepens the learning curve, yielding 10x-equivalent compute gains without additional hardware.
Compute scarcity is worsening—H100 prices up ~40% from lows, reasoning models use 8x more tokens (projected 5x more), and frontier API access may become constrained.
DatologyAI's refinery framework has four stages: clean, curate, create, and compose—sequencing across stages matters as much as any single step.
There is no universal golden dataset; data optimality is always relative to target output tasks and requires diversity and correct mixing.
VLM curation alone delivered ~14 absolute percentage point improvement and matched Qwen 3.5 4B with ~145x less training compute and ~35x fewer inference flops per correct answer.
Cross-lingual transfer: curating English data improves non-English performance, with transfer magnitude correlated to language similarity between English and the target language.
Synthetic 'rephrasing' avoids model collapse by deriving all content from source documents; selecting high-quality documents for rephrasing is critical.
Thomson Reuters gained ~5 legal-bench points with <1% of pre-training budget, and post-training effectiveness nearly tripled when applied to the mid-trained model.
Arcee's Trinity Large reached open-frontier performance on 17T curated public tokens for under $20M total, proving custom frontier-quality models are achievable without hundreds of millions.
Small curated models enable predictable scaling and derisking of large training runs—the 50x-larger model fell on the same scaling line.

concepts.name: Scaling Law Exponent Modification via Data Selection
concepts.explanation: The finding from the NeurIPS 2022 paper 'Beyond neural scaling laws' that data selection/pruning can change the exponent of the power-law scaling relationship between dataset size and model error, potentially achieving better-than-power-law (exponential) scaling.
concepts.importance: This is the theoretical foundation for the entire talk. If data selection can change the scaling law exponent, then data quality is not just an incremental improvement—it fundamentally alters the compute-performance tradeoff, making it a true multiplier rather than a constant factor.

concepts.name: Data Quality as Compute Multiplier
concepts.explanation: The thesis that improving training data quality steepens the learning curve, so the same compute budget yields dramatically better performance, or equivalent performance at a fraction of the compute cost—effectively multiplying available compute.
concepts.importance: This is the central argument of the talk and reframes data engineering from a preprocessing concern to a strategic compute optimization lever. It provides the economic rationale for investing in data curation over buying more hardware.

concepts.name: Marginal Information Gain Per Token
concepts.explanation: The principle of maximizing the novel information each training token contributes to the model, rather than maximizing raw token count. Data optimality is always relative to target tasks and requires diversity and correct mixing.
concepts.importance: This is the guiding principle behind all curation decisions. It explains why redundant or irrelevant data wastes compute and why there is no universal golden dataset—optimal data depends on what the model needs to learn.

concepts.name: Synthetic Data via Rephrasing
concepts.explanation: A synthetic data generation approach that converts high-quality source documents into hundreds of template formats (e.g., true/false questions, summaries) where all information derives from the source document, avoiding model collapse because the rephrasing model need only transform accurately—not understand concepts.
concepts.importance: Addresses the data scarcity problem while avoiding the model collapse failure mode that plagues other synthetic data approaches. The key insight is that source-faithful rephrasing scales diversity without introducing compounding errors.

concepts.name: Model Collapse Avoidance
concepts.explanation: The degradation that occurs when models are trained on synthetic data generated by other models, causing compounding errors and loss of diversity. DatologyAI's rephrasing approach avoids this by ensuring all synthetic content is grounded in real source documents.
concepts.importance: Model collapse is a critical failure mode in synthetic data pipelines. Understanding how rephrasing avoids it is essential for building reliable synthetic data generation systems at scale.

concepts.name: Cross-Lingual Transfer from Curated English Data
concepts.explanation: The finding that curating English training data improves non-English model performance, with the magnitude of transfer strongly correlated to the similarity between English and the target language. Curating non-English data also benefits English, though to a smaller degree.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates that data curation has non-obvious multi-modal benefits. This finding means teams can improve multilingual performance without proportionally increasing multilingual training data, a significant compute saving.

concepts.name: Mid-Training Synergy with Post-Training
concepts.explanation: The finding that post-training (instruction tuning, RLHF) is significantly more effective when applied to a mid-trained model (domain-adapted via continued pre-training) than to a default instruction-tuned model. Thomson Reuters saw post-training gains nearly triple.
concepts.importance: Challenges the common practice of treating training stages as independent. The synergy means mid-training is not just a domain adaptation step but a foundation that amplifies all subsequent training, changing how teams should plan their training pipelines.

concepts.name: Catastrophic Forgetting Prevention During Domain Adaptation
concepts.explanation: The risk that domain-specific mid-training causes the model to forget general capabilities. Mitigated by ensuring the majority of mid-training data represents the pre-training distribution, so general capabilities actually improve alongside domain-specific gains.
concepts.importance: A critical practical concern for any team doing domain adaptation. The Thomson Reuters case shows that with proper data composition, domain adaptation can improve both domain-specific and general capabilities simultaneously.

concepts.name: Pareto Frontier Improvement via Curation
concepts.explanation: Curation alone can push models beyond the Pareto frontier defined by existing models at similar or larger scales, as demonstrated by DatologyAI's VLM results exceeding the frontier defined by Qwen 3 series, Intern VL, and others.
concepts.importance: Shows that data quality is not just about matching performance more efficiently—it can actually exceed what is achievable with uncured data at any compute level, redefining what is possible at each scale.

concepts.name: Inference Efficiency from Curated Training Data
concepts.explanation: Models trained on better-curated data produce more concise outputs, achieving similar performance with ~35x fewer inference flops per correct answer, reducing both training and serving costs.
concepts.importance: Extends the compute multiplier argument to inference. Data quality affects not just training efficiency but also deployment cost, making the business case for curation even stronger.

concepts.name: Compute Scarcity Dynamics
concepts.explanation: The economic context driving the need for data quality: H100 prices reversed decline and are ~40% above lows, reasoning models use ~8x more tokens than non-reasoning models (projected to 5x again), and frontier API access may become constrained.
concepts.importance: Provides the economic urgency for the talk's thesis. Without compute scarcity, data quality is a nice-to-have; with scarcity, it becomes a strategic necessity that determines which teams can afford to train competitive models.

concepts.name: Data Repetition vs. Low-Quality Data Tradeoff
concepts.explanation: The principle that it is almost always better to repeat high-quality data than to show low-quality data, up to a threshold. This challenges the intuition that more unique data is always better.
concepts.importance: A counterintuitive but practically important guideline for data pipeline design. It means teams should prefer smaller, higher-quality datasets with controlled repetition over larger datasets containing noise.

concepts.name: Data Refinery Pipeline (Clean, Curate, Create, Compose)
concepts.explanation: A four-stage data engineering framework for transforming raw data into high-quality training datasets: clean (heuristic filters, benchmark decontamination), curate (quality classifiers, taxonomy balancing, redundancy reduction, task distribution matching), create (synthetic data generation via rephrasing), and compose (sequencing across training stages).
concepts.importance: This is the core engineering methodology presented in the talk. It provides a structured, reproducible pipeline architecture that teams can implement to systematically improve training data quality, directly translating to compute savings and better model performance.

concepts.name: Benchmark Decontamination
concepts.explanation: The process of removing benchmark evaluation data from training datasets to prevent contamination that would inflate model performance metrics and make results difficult to interpret.
concepts.importance: Critical for trustworthy evaluation. Without decontamination, benchmark scores become unreliable, and the true capability of models cannot be assessed. Morcos identifies contamination as a serious industry problem.

concepts.name: Semantic Deduplication / Redundancy Reduction
concepts.explanation: Removing semantically duplicate or near-duplicate data points from training datasets to reduce redundancy and ensure each training example provides marginal information gain rather than repeating known signals.
concepts.importance: Redundant data wastes compute by repeatedly showing the model information it has already learned. Deduplication is a key curation step that directly improves compute efficiency by maximizing novel signal per token.

concepts.name: Task Distribution Matching
concepts.explanation: Aligning the distribution of training data across task categories with the distribution of target evaluation or deployment tasks, ensuring the model is trained on data proportions that match intended use cases.
concepts.importance: Ensures models are optimized for their actual deployment scenarios rather than over-fitting to whatever distribution the raw web data happens to contain. This is a key engineering decision that affects real-world model utility.

concepts.name: Data Sequencing Across Training Stages
concepts.explanation: The practice of composing and ordering data across different training stages (pre-training, mid-training, post-training) as a continuous curriculum, rather than treating each stage independently.
concepts.importance: The Thomson Reuters case demonstrates that mid-training and post-training are synergistic—post-training gains nearly tripled when applied to a mid-trained model. Sequencing decisions across stages are as important as any single curation step.

concepts.name: Predictable Scaling from Small Curated Models
concepts.explanation: Training small models on curated data to establish a scaling law line that accurately predicts the performance of much larger models trained with 50x more compute, enabling teams to derisk expensive large training runs.
concepts.importance: This engineering methodology allows teams to validate data curation strategies cheaply before committing to frontier-scale training. Arcee's two 1T-token models predicted the 17T-token Trinity Large's performance, proving the approach works at scale.

concepts.name: Multi-Axis Data Scoring at Peta-Byte Scale
concepts.explanation: Engineering systems that score training data across multiple quality dimensions (relevance, diversity, quality, task alignment) at peta-byte scale, requiring distributed computing infrastructure and efficient scoring algorithms.
concepts.importance: Morcos frames data curation as a frontier research engineering problem precisely because scoring data across many axes at peta-byte scale is a systems engineering challenge, not just an algorithmic one. This is the infrastructure that makes the refinery framework operational.

concepts.name: Quality Classification Pipelines
concepts.explanation: Automated classifier systems that score and filter training documents based on quality metrics, replacing manual curation with scalable, reproducible quality assessment.
concepts.importance: Enables data curation at the scale required for frontier model training, where manual review is infeasible. Quality classifiers are a core component of the curate stage and directly determine which data enters the training pipeline.

sections.title: Data Quality as a Compute Multiplier
sections.summary: Morcos introduces DatologyAI and the core thesis: compute is increasingly scarce (H100 prices up 40%, reasoning models using 8x more tokens with 5x projected growth, frontier APIs facing potential limits), making data quality the key lever. Better data steepens the learning curve, effectively multiplying compute.

sections.title: Maximizing Signal Per Token
sections.summary: The goal is maximizing marginal information gain per data point. There is no universal golden dataset—optimality depends on target tasks. Data must be relevant, diverse, and correctly mixed. The same x-axis represents data, compute, time, and dollars.

sections.title: The Oil Refinery Framework: Clean, Curate, Create, Compose
sections.summary: DatologyAI refines existing tokens rather than sourcing new ones. Cleaning involves heuristic filters and benchmark decontamination. Curation uses quality classifiers, taxonomy balancing, redundancy reduction, upsampling/downsampling, and task distribution matching. Synthetic data augments diversity and scale. Composition sequences data across training stages.

sections.title: Research Foundation and Proof of Principle
sections.summary: Half of DatologyAI's team are researchers. The foundational paper 'Beyond Scaling Laws' (NeurIPS best paper, written at Meta) showed data selection changes the scaling law exponent, proving that redundant or unnecessary data wastes compute.

sections.title: VLM Results: Curation Alone Beats Larger Models
sections.summary: Using the ~25B token Mammoth dataset for fusion adapter training, curation yielded ~14 absolute percentage point improvement and matched Qwen 3.5 4B with ~145x less training compute. Curated models also produced more concise answers and achieved similar performance with ~35x fewer inference flops per correct answer.

sections.title: Multilingual Gains and Cross-Lingual Transfer
sections.summary: Using only 8% multilingual tokens, curated data significantly outperforms larger models on multilingual MMLU. Cross-lingual transfer is observed: curating English data alone improves non-English accuracy, with transfer magnitude correlated to similarity between English and the target language. Curating non-English data also benefits English performance, though to a smaller degree.

sections.title: Predictable Scaling from Small Curated Models
sections.summary: Two dense Llama-style models trained for 1T tokens on curated data define a scaling line that Arcee's Trinity Large (17T tokens, 50x more compute) falls directly on, demonstrating that proper data curation and token-scarcity simulation enable predictable scaling and derisking of large training runs.

sections.title: Synthetic Data via Rephrasing
sections.summary: DatologyAI's 'rephrasing' approach converts high-quality source documents into hundreds of template formats (e.g., true/false questions). Since all information derives from the source document, model collapse is avoided, and the rephrasing model need only transform accurately—not understand concepts. Selecting high-quality documents for rephrasing is critical; random selection yields poor results. The method applies to any proprietary data within customer environments.

sections.title: Thomson Reuters: Mid-Training Synergy with Post-Training
sections.summary: Mid-training on 100B tokens (less than 1% of pre-training budget) combining Thomson Reuters proprietary legal data with public data improved LegalBench by ~5 percentage points without catastrophic forgetting—general capabilities also rose because the majority of data represented the pre-training distribution. Critically, post-training gains nearly tripled when applied to the mid-trained model versus the default instruction-tuned model, demonstrating training stages should be treated synergistically.

sections.title: Arcee Trinity Large: Open-Frontier on Public Data
sections.summary: Arcee trained Trinity Large on 17 trillion tokens curated entirely from public datasets—no proprietary data, no closed-model usage. The model matches GLM5 and Kimmy on many tasks and outperforms Claude on some. Total cost including compute, salaries, and R&D was under $20 million, disproving the notion that frontier-quality models require hundreds of millions. The Arcee team had not trained a model before partnering with DatologyAI.

sections.title: Closing: Data Quality as the Underleveraged Multiplier
sections.summary: Morcos closes by emphasizing signal per token over raw token count. It is almost always better to repeat high-quality data than show low-quality data, up to a threshold. Data quality remains the single most underleveraged compute multiplier—it is cheaper to manufacture high-quality data than buy more compute. This is a frontier research engineering problem requiring multi-axis data scoring at peta-byte scale.

organization.name: DatologyAI
organization.summary: DatologyAI is an AI data curation company founded in 2023 and headquartered in Redwood City, California. The company builds modality-agnostic tools to automatically select and curate the best training data for deep learning models, identifying redundant, noisy, or harmful data points without requiring labels. CEO and co-founder Ari Morcos previously worked at Meta AI (FAIR) where he co-authored the NeurIPS 2022 Outstanding Paper 'Beyond neural scaling laws: beating power law scaling via data pruning.' The company has raised approximately $57.6M in total funding (Seed $11.7M in February 2024, Series A $46M in May 2024 led by Felicis) and employs approximately 49 people across the United States and Switzerland. Approximately half the team are researchers. The platform implements a four-stage refinery framework: clean (heuristic filters, benchmark decontamination), curate (quality classifiers, taxonomy balancing, redundancy reduction, task distribution matching), create (synthetic data via rephrasing), and compose (sequencing across training stages).

technologies.label: DatologyAI Data Curation Platform (Data Refinery)
technologies.summary: DatologyAI's platform implements a four-stage 'data refinery' pipeline—clean (heuristic filters, benchmark decontamination), curate (quality classifiers, taxonomy balancing, redundancy reduction, task distribution matching), create (synthetic data via rephrasing), and compose (sequencing across training stages, continuous curricula)—that transforms raw data into high-quality training datasets. The core thesis is that data quality acts as a compute multiplier by steepening the learning curve, yielding equivalent model performance at a fraction of the compute cost. Proof points include VLMs matching Qwen 3.5 4B with ~145x less training compute via curation alone, multilingual gains with only 8% multilingual tokens, and Thomson Reuters gaining ~5 LegalBench points with <1% of pre-training budget.
technologies.role: This is the primary technology of the talk. Morcos presents DatologyAI's platform as a data refinery that transforms raw data into high-quality training datasets, with the four-stage framework as the core engineering methodology.

technologies.label: Data Pruning for Scaling Law Exponent Modification
technologies.primary: Data Pruning for Scaling Law Exponent Modification
technologies.summary: The foundational technique demonstrated in the NeurIPS 2022 Outstanding Paper 'Beyond neural scaling laws: beating power law scaling via data pruning,' co-authored by Ari Morcos at Meta/FAIR with Stanford and University of Tübingen. Data pruning/selection can change the exponent of the power-law scaling relationship between dataset size and model error, potentially achieving better-than-power-law (exponential) scaling. This proves that data quality is not just an incremental improvement but fundamentally alters the compute-performance tradeoff, making it a true multiplier rather than a constant factor. This research is the intellectual foundation for DatologyAI's entire approach.
technologies.role: Provides the theoretical foundation for the entire talk. Morcos cites this NeurIPS 2022 Outstanding Paper as proof that data selection can change the scaling law exponent, which is why data quality acts as a compute multiplier rather than a constant factor.

technologies.label: Synthetic Data Generation via Rephrasing
technologies.summary: A synthetic data generation technique that converts high-quality source documents into hundreds of template formats (e.g., true/false questions, summaries). Since all information derives from the source document, model collapse is avoided—the rephrasing model need only transform accurately, not understand concepts. Selecting high-quality documents for rephrasing is critical; random selection yields poor results. The method applies to any proprietary data within customer environments. Morcos also argues it is almost always better to repeat high-quality data than to show low-quality data, up to a threshold, further motivating synthetic augmentation of curated data.
technologies.role: Presented as the 'create' stage of the four-stage refinery framework. Morcos demonstrates the approach with a concrete example and explains why it avoids model collapse—a critical failure mode in synthetic data pipelines.

technologies.label: Trinity Large (Arcee AI)
technologies.summary: Arcee AI's 398B/400B parameter sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 13B active parameters per token, trained on 17 trillion DatologyAI-curated public tokens from a 20T mix including 8T+ synthetic tokens. Trinity Large matches GLM5 and Kimmy on many tasks and outperforms Claude on some, all for under $20M total cost including compute, salaries, data, storage, and operations. It demonstrates that frontier-quality models are achievable without proprietary data, closed-model usage, or hundreds of millions in compute. Two smaller 1T-token dense Llama-style models trained on curated data predicted Trinity Large's performance, falling directly on the same scaling line despite 50x more compute.
technologies.role: Central proof point in the talk's closing section. Morcos presents Trinity Large as evidence that DatologyAI's data curation enables frontier-quality models on public data alone for under $20M, disproving the notion that frontier models require hundreds of millions in compute.
